intended_object: The slope represented by a primitive class v ∈ M ≅ H₁(T; ℤ), i.e. the class ±v of v in the set of primitive classes taken modulo sign. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation (Rolfsen, Ch. 9).
explanation:
`Slope M` is the quotient of the subtype of primitive elements of M by the relation a = b ∨ a = -b. The module docstring says "primitive" means that some ℤ-linear functional sends the element to 1. `Slope.mk v h` sends the primitive vector v to its equivalence class, which is exactly "the slope represented by v", i.e. the unordered pair {v, -v}.

The library proves `mk_eq_mk_iff`: two primitive vectors give the same slope exactly when they agree up to sign. That is the expected behaviour. Primitivity is required as a proof argument, so there are no junk-value issues.

The construction is stated for an arbitrary ℤ-module M, which is the natural basis-free generality for this notion. Mathlib has no notion of slopes or projectivized primitive vectors to compare against.
